q: Let \(A=\begin{bmatrix}4&-3&3\\1&-4&0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\-1&-2\\5&5\end{bmatrix}\). Find the (1,1) entry of \(AB\).
Row 1 of A times column 1 of B: 4(1) + (-3)((-1)) + 3(5) = 22.
Let \(A=\begin{bmatrix}5&3&4\\5&3&-2\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B=\begin{bmatrix}2&4\\-2&-3\\3&4\end{bmatrix}\). Find the (2,2) entry of \((AB)^{T}\).
The (2,2) entry of \((AB)^{T}\) is the (2,2) entry of AB: row 2 of A times column 2 of B = 3. (Same as \(B^{T}A^{T}\).)
What is the largest possible rank of a 2×3 matrix?
Rank cannot exceed the number of rows or the number of columns, so the maximum is min(2, 3) = 2.

The point \(P(9, -1, -8)\) lies on \(\overline{AB}\) between \(A(3, 2, 1)\) and \(B(13, -3, -14)\). Find \(AP:PB\).
Compare one coordinate: \(\overrightarrow{AP}=P-A=6\hat i-3\hat j-9\hat k\) and \(\overrightarrow{AB}=10\hat i-5\hat j-15\hat k\), so \(AP=\dfrac{3}{5}AB\), i.e. \(AP:PB=3:2\).

Find the area of the triangle with vertices \((1, 3)\), \((-4, -1)\), \((-3, 2)\).
Treat the points as \((x,y,0)\). \(\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=-11\hat k\), so the area is \(\tfrac12|-11|=\frac{11}{2}\).
Find the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are \(\vec a=4\hat i+2\hat j+4\hat k\) and \(\vec b=-\hat j+2\hat k\).
Area \(=|\vec a\times\vec b|\). \(\vec a\times\vec b=8\hat i-8\hat j-4\hat k\), so area \(=\sqrt{144}=12\).
If \(|\vec a|=8\), \(|\vec b|=2\) and \(\vec a\cdot\vec b=8\), find \(|\vec a\times\vec b|^2\).
Lagrange identity: \(|\vec a\times\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2-(\vec a\cdot\vec b)^2=64\cdot4-(8)^2=192\).

Treat the points as \((x,y,0)\). \(\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=-4\hat k\), so the area is \(\tfrac12|-4|=2\).
Find \(\sin\theta\), where \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec a=-10\hat i-5\hat j+10\hat k\) and \(\vec b=-11\hat i+2\hat j-10\hat k\).
\(\sin\theta=\dfrac{|\vec a\times\vec b|}{|\vec a||\vec b|}\). \(\vec a\times\vec b=30\hat i-210\hat j-75\hat k\), \(|\vec a|=15\), \(|\vec b|=15\), so \(\sin\theta=1\).
A constant force \(\vec F=-\hat i+\hat j-3\hat k\) moves a particle from \(P(1, 3, -1)\) to \(Q(1, 1, 1)\). Find the work done.
Displacement \(\vec S=\overrightarrow{PQ}=Q-P=-2\hat j+2\hat k\). Work \(W=\vec F\cdot\vec S=-8\) (units of work).
Find the position vector of the midpoint of \(A(-2, 0, -1)\) and \(B(-2, -6, 1)\).
If \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec a=5\hat i+10\hat j+10\hat k\) and \(\vec b=7\hat i+6\hat j+6\hat k\), find \(\cos\theta\).
Find the moment of the force \(\vec F=-4\hat i-4\hat j-3\hat k\) acting at the point \(P(-1, 3, 1)\) about the origin.
\(\vec r=\overrightarrow{OP}=P-O=-\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k\); \(\vec M=\vec r\times\vec F=-5\hat i-7\hat j+16\hat k\). (Order matters: \(\vec r\) first, then \(\vec F\).)
Which vector is parallel to \(\vec a=3\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k\)?
Parallel vectors are scalar multiples: \(\vec b=k\vec a\). Only \(9\hat i-3\hat j+6\hat k=3\vec a\) has all three ratios equal to \(3\).
\(\vec a=-2\hat i+\hat j+\hat k\), \(\vec b=3\hat i-2\hat j-\hat k\). The angle between them is
\(\vec a\cdot\vec b=-9\). Positive dot product \(\Rightarrow\) acute angle, zero \(\Rightarrow\) \(90^\circ\), negative \(\Rightarrow\) obtuse.
Find \(\lambda\) so that \(\vec a=-\hat i-4\hat j+2\hat k\) is parallel to \(\vec b=2\hat i+8\hat j+\lambda\hat k\).
Parallel means \(\vec b=k\vec a\), i.e. equal ratios of components. From the first component \(k=\dfrac{2}{-1}=-2\), so \(\lambda=k\cdot(2)=-4\).
Find the position vector of the centroid of the triangle with vertices \(A(1, 2, -3)\), \(B(4, 2, 5)\), \(C(-2, -1, 4)\).
The centroid divides each median in the ratio \(2:1\): \(\vec g=\dfrac{\vec a+\vec b+\vec c}{3}=\dfrac{(3, 3, 6)}{3}=\hat i+\hat j+2\hat k\).
A vector makes angles \(30^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\) with the \(x\)- and \(y\)-axes. Find the angle it makes with the \(z\)-axis (acute).
Find the position vector of the centroid of the triangle with vertices \(A(4, -2, -1)\), \(B(3, -5, 1)\), \(C(2, 4, 0)\).
The centroid divides each median in the ratio \(2:1\): \(\vec g=\dfrac{\vec a+\vec b+\vec c}{3}=\dfrac{(9, -3, 0)}{3}=3\hat i-\hat j\).
Find the direction cosines \((l, m, n)\) of \(\vec r=4\hat i-6\hat j+12\hat k\).
A constant force \(\vec F=2\hat j-2\hat k\) moves a particle from \(P(-2, 0, -2)\) to \(Q(2, -2, -2)\). Find the work done.
Displacement \(\vec S=\overrightarrow{PQ}=Q-P=4\hat i-2\hat j\). Work \(W=\vec F\cdot\vec S=-4\) (units of work).
Find \(\sin\theta\), where \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec a=-2\hat i-10\hat j-11\hat k\) and \(\vec b=-6\hat i-3\hat j-6\hat k\).
\(\sin\theta=\dfrac{|\vec a\times\vec b|}{|\vec a||\vec b|}\). \(\vec a\times\vec b=27\hat i+54\hat j-54\hat k\), \(|\vec a|=15\), \(|\vec b|=9\), so \(\sin\theta=\frac{3}{5}\).

\(v_x=u\cos\phi=20\cos60^\circ=10\) m/s (constant, since no horizontal force acts).
Find \(\lambda\) so that \(\vec a\times\vec b=\vec 0\) for \(\vec a=3\hat i+3\hat j+2\hat k\) and \(\vec b=-6\hat i+\lambda\hat j-4\hat k\).
\(\vec a\times\vec b=\vec 0\) means the vectors are parallel: \(\vec b=-2\vec a\), so \(\lambda=-2\cdot(3)=-6\).
Find \(\vec a\cdot\vec b\times\vec c\) for \(\vec a=3\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k\), \(\vec b=-3\hat i+\hat k\), \(\vec c=-2\hat j+\hat k\).
Find \(\vec a\times\vec b\) for \(\vec a=-2\hat i+\hat j+3\hat k\), \(\vec b=3\hat i+4\hat j\).
\(\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\ -2&1&3\\ 3&4&0\end{vmatrix}=-12\hat i+9\hat j-11\hat k\) (signs \(+,-,+\) along the top row).
Find the volume of the tetrahedron with vertices \(A(0, 0, -3)\), \(B(2, 2, -5)\), \(C(3, -2, -5)\), \(D(-1, 1, -2)\).

\(\overrightarrow{AB}=2\hat i+2\hat j-2\hat k\), \(\overrightarrow{AC}=3\hat i-2\hat j-2\hat k\), \(\overrightarrow{AD}=-\hat i+\hat j+\hat k\); determinant \(=-4\). Volume \(=\tfrac16|-4|=\frac{2}{3}\).
For which value of \(t\) are \(A(3, -4, 3)\), \(B(1, -1, 6)\) and \(C(-1, 2, t)\) collinear?
\(\overrightarrow{AB}=-2\hat i+3\hat j+3\hat k\) and \(\overrightarrow{AC}\) must be parallel to it. The first two components give \(\overrightarrow{AC}=2\,\overrightarrow{AB}\), so \(t=z_A+2(3)=9\).
Find \(\lambda\) so that \(\vec a=2\hat i\), \(\vec b=3\hat i-\hat j-3\hat k\), \(\vec c=3\hat i+3\hat j+\lambda\hat k\) are coplanar.
Coplanar \(\Leftrightarrow\) \(\vec a\cdot\vec b\times\vec c=0\). Expanding the determinant gives \(18 - 2 lam=0\), so \(\lambda=9\).
Two direction cosines of a vector are \(l=\frac{9}{11}\) and \(m=\frac{2}{11}\). Find \(n^2\).

Find the position vector of the midpoint of \(A(-3, 1, 1)\) and \(B(-7, 1, 1)\).
Midpoint \(=\dfrac{\vec a+\vec b}{2}=\dfrac{(-10, 2, 2)}{2}=-5\hat i+\hat j+\hat k\).

The point \(P(2, -5, 11)\) lies on \(\overline{AB}\) between \(A(-4, 4, 2)\) and \(B(6, -11, 17)\). Find \(AP:PB\).

Find the moment of the force \(\vec F=-3\hat i+4\hat j+3\hat k\) acting at the point \(P(4, -2, -4)\) about the origin.
\(\vec r=\overrightarrow{OP}=P-O=4\hat i-2\hat j-4\hat k\); \(\vec M=\vec r\times\vec F=10\hat i+10\hat k\). (Order matters: \(\vec r\) first, then \(\vec F\).)
The point \(P\) divides \(\overline{AB}\) externally in the ratio \(AP:PB=2:3\), where \(A(1, 4, -1)\) and \(B(-2, 7, 2)\). Find \(\overrightarrow{OP}\).
External division: \(\vec r=\dfrac{m\vec b-n\vec a}{m-n}=\dfrac{2(-2, 7, 2)-3(1, 4, -1)}{-1}=7\hat i-2\hat j-7\hat k\).

parallel to the third side and half as long

\(\vec a\times\vec b=2\hat i\) is perpendicular to both; its magnitude is \(2\). Divide by it: \(\hat i\) (the negative of this is the other unit vector).
Find \(\vec a\times\vec b\) for \(\vec a=3\hat i+4\hat j-4\hat k\), \(\vec b=\hat i+\hat j+\hat k\).
\(\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\ 3&4&-4\\ 1&1&1\end{vmatrix}=8\hat i-7\hat j-\hat k\) (signs \(+,-,+\) along the top row).
A stone is thrown with initial speed 50 m/s at \(60^\circ\) above the horizontal. Find its horizontal velocity component (m/s).
\(v_x=u\cos\phi=50\cos60^\circ=25\) m/s (constant, since no horizontal force acts).
The point \(P\) divides \(\overline{AB}\) internally in the ratio \(AP:PB=2:1\), where \(A(-2, 1, 0)\) and \(B(-5, -8, -3)\). Find \(\overrightarrow{OP}\).
\(\vec r=\dfrac{n\vec a+m\vec b}{m+n}=\dfrac{1(-2, 1, 0)+2(-5, -8, -3)}{3}=-4\hat i-5\hat j-2\hat k\). (The second vector \(\vec b\) is multiplied by the first number \(m\).)
If \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec a=-9\hat i+12\hat j-8\hat k\) and \(\vec b=-11\hat i+2\hat j-10\hat k\), find \(\cos\theta\).
Find \(\vec a\times\vec b\) for \(\vec a=-5\hat i+6\hat j-4\hat k\), \(\vec b=6\hat i-4\hat j-5\hat k\).
\(\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\ -5&6&-4\\ 6&-4&-5\end{vmatrix}=-46\hat i-49\hat j-16\hat k\) (signs \(+,-,+\) along the top row).
A constant force \(\vec F=-2\hat i+2\hat j-3\hat k\) moves a particle from \(P(3, -1, -2)\) to \(Q(-3, 1, -1)\). Find the work done.
Displacement \(\vec S=\overrightarrow{PQ}=Q-P=-6\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k\). Work \(W=\vec F\cdot\vec S=13\) (units of work).
Find the vector projection of \(\vec b=4\hat i+\hat j+2\hat k\) on \(\vec a=8\hat i-8\hat j-4\hat k\), i.e. \(\left(\dfrac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec a|}\right)\hat a\).

Find \(\lambda\) so that \(\vec a\times\vec b=\vec 0\) for \(\vec a=\hat i+\hat j+4\hat k\) and \(\vec b=-2\hat i+\lambda\hat j-8\hat k\).
\(\vec a\times\vec b=\vec 0\) means the vectors are parallel: \(\vec b=-2\vec a\), so \(\lambda=-2\cdot(1)=-2\).
Find the volume of the tetrahedron with vertices \(A(3, 1, -2)\), \(B(0, 4, -1)\), \(C(1, 3, -5)\), \(D(3, 4, 1)\).

\(\overrightarrow{AB}=-3\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k\), \(\overrightarrow{AC}=-2\hat i+2\hat j-3\hat k\), \(\overrightarrow{AD}=3\hat j+3\hat k\); determinant \(=-33\). Volume \(=\tfrac16|-33|=\frac{11}{2}\).

The point \(P\) divides \(\overline{AB}\) externally in the ratio \(AP:PB=3:1\), where \(A(1, -3, -1)\) and \(B(-3, -5, -7)\). Find \(\overrightarrow{OP}\).

Find the area of the triangle with vertices \((-4, -2)\), \((1, -2)\), \((-3, 0)\).
Treat the points as \((x,y,0)\). \(\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=10\hat k\), so the area is \(\tfrac12|10|=5\).
If \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec a=3\hat i-6\hat j-6\hat k\) and \(\vec b=10\hat i-2\hat j-11\hat k\), find \(\cos\theta\).
The point \(P\) divides \(\overline{AB}\) internally in the ratio \(AP:PB=3:1\), where \(A(4, 3, 4)\) and \(B(-8, 11, -8)\). Find \(\overrightarrow{OP}\).

The point \(P\) divides \(\overline{AB}\) internally in the ratio \(AP:PB=3:1\), where \(A(1, -2, 2)\) and \(B(13, 10, 6)\). Find \(\overrightarrow{OP}\).
\(\vec r=\dfrac{n\vec a+m\vec b}{m+n}=\dfrac{1(1, -2, 2)+3(13, 10, 6)}{4}=10\hat i+7\hat j+5\hat k\). (The second vector \(\vec b\) is multiplied by the first number \(m\).)
If \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec a=-9\hat i+8\hat j+12\hat k\) and \(\vec b=-4\hat i+4\hat j+2\hat k\), find \(\cos\theta\).
\(ABCD\) is a parallelogram (vertices in this order) with \(A(2, -5, -2)\), \(B(2, 0, -5)\), \(C(-2, 5, 3)\). Find \(D\).
The diagonals bisect each other, so \(\dfrac{\vec a+\vec c}{2}=\dfrac{\vec b+\vec d}{2}\) and \(\vec d=\vec a+\vec c-\vec b=-2\hat i+6\hat k\).
Find the area of the triangle with vertices \((-1, -1)\), \((-3, -2)\), \((0, -1)\).

Find the remainder when \(z^{4} - 5 z^{3} + 6 z^{2} - 6 z + 3\) is divided by \(z + 3\).

The divisor \(z + 3\) is zero when \(z=-3\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-3)=291\). (A common slip is to use \(p(3)\) = \(-15\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
The volume of a rectangular box is \(88\) cubic units. The length is 7 more than the height and the width is 2 less than the height. Find the longest side of the box.

A cubic with three distinct real zeros splits into how many linear factors?
Each real zero gives one linear factor: three zeros, three factors.
The polynomial \(k + 2 x^{4} - 3 x^{3} - 6 x^{2} - 6 x\) leaves remainder \(205\) when divided by \(x + 3\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-3)\). Substituting: \(k + 207=205\), which gives \(k=-2\). Always substitute back to check.

Find the remainder when \(3 x^{4} - 2 x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 5 x + 7\) is divided by \(x - 2\).
The divisor \(x - 2\) is zero when \(x=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=21\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(73\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)

After finding one linear factor of a cubic, the remaining factor is a

Divide \(x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 4 x + 13\) by \(x - 2\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(5\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(x^{2} - 4\) and the remainder is \(5\). Check: \((x - 2)(x^{2} - 4)+5=x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 4 x + 13\).
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(2, -5, -4\).

Find the remainder when \(3 x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + x + 9\) is divided by \(x - 1\).

The polynomial \(k y^{2} + 2 y^{3} - 3 y + 5\) leaves remainder \(10\) when divided by \(y + 1\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-1)\). Substituting: \(k + 6=10\), which gives \(k=4\). Always substitute back to check.
Divide \(2 t^{3} - 8 t^{2} + 9 t - 1\) by \(t - 1\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(2\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 t^{2} - 6 t + 3\) and the remainder is \(2\). Check: \((t - 1)(2 t^{2} - 6 t + 3)+2=2 t^{3} - 8 t^{2} + 9 t - 1\).
If \(x + 2\) and \(x + 3\) are both factors of \(a x^{2} + b x + x^{3} - 6\), find \(b\).
\(p(-2)=0\) and \(p(-3)=0\) give two linear equations in \(a\) and \(b\). Solving: \(a=4,\ b=1\).
Find the remainder when \(3 x^{4} + 2 x^{3} + 4 x^{2} + 7 x - 6\) is divided by \(4 x + 3\).
Set \(4 x + 3=0\): \(x=- \frac{3}{4}\). Remainder \(=p(- \frac{3}{4})=- \frac{2277}{256}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
The volume of a rectangular box is \(96\) cubic units. The width is 3 times the height and the length is 2 more than the width. Find the longest side of the box.

Find the remainder when \(t^{3} - 2 t^{2} + 5 t - 1\) is divided by \(t - 1\).
The divisor \(t - 1\) is zero when \(t=1\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(1)=3\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-1)\) = \(-9\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Without long division, find the remainder when \(3 x^{3} + 2 x^{2} + 2 x + 7\) is divided by \(x-1\).
Divisor \(x-1\) gives \(x=1\). The remainder \(p(1)=14\) is the sum of all the coefficients: no division needed.

\(\text{volume}=\text{area of floor}\times\text{height}\), so floor area = volume ÷ height. \(x^{3} + 10 x^{2} + 27 x + 18\) ÷ \(x+6\) = \(x^{2} + 4 x + 3\).

A polynomial is divided by a polynomial of degree \(1\). What is the highest possible degree of the remainder?
The degree of the remainder is always less than the degree of the divisor, so at most \(1-1=0\). (A degree-0 remainder is a constant.)

Degrees subtract under division: the quotient has degree m − n.
A room has volume \(x^{3} + 13 x^{2} + 47 x + 35\) cubic feet and height \(x+7\) feet. Find the area of its floor.
\(\text{volume}=\text{area of floor}\times\text{height}\), so floor area = volume ÷ height. \(x^{3} + 13 x^{2} + 47 x + 35\) ÷ \(x+7\) = \(x^{2} + 6 x + 5\).
The height (in feet) of a ball after \(t\) seconds is \(h(t)=- 16 t^{2} + 80 t + 6\). Find its height after \(3\) seconds.
\(h(3)=-16(3)^2+80(3)+6=102\). By the Remainder Theorem this is also the remainder of \(h(t)\) divided by \(t-3\).

degree of quotient = degree of dividend − degree of divisor = \(5-3=2\).

The polynomial \(2 k + 2 y^{3} + 3 y^{2} + 3 y\) leaves remainder \(-26\) when divided by \(y + 3\). Find \(k\).

Find the remainder when \(3 y^{4} + 8 y^{3} + 3 y + 1\) is divided by \(y - 3\).

Without long division, find the remainder when \(3 x^{4} - x^{3} - 2 x^{2} + 3\) is divided by \(x-1\).

A polynomial of degree \(4\) is divided by a polynomial of degree \(2\). What is the degree of the quotient?

Find the remainder when \(x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 4 x - 7\) is divided by \(x^{2} + x - 2\).

\(x--4\) is a factor (since \(p(-4)=0\)). Dividing leaves a quadratic whose roots are \(1\text{ and }2\). The largest zero is \(2\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(x - 3\) is a factor of \(2 k x + x^{3} + 3\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-5)=0\) so \(x + 5\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 5)(x + 3)(2 x - 5)\). Check by expanding.
Find the remainder when \(x^{4} - 3 x^{3} - 7 x^{2} + 4 x + 1\) is divided by \(x + 3\).

The divisor \(x + 3\) is zero when \(x=-3\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-3)=88\). (A common slip is to use \(p(3)\) = \(-50\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
If \(x + 1\) and \(x + 2\) are both factors of \(a x^{2} + b x + x^{3} + 4\), find \(b\).
\(p(-1)=0\) and \(p(-2)=0\) give two linear equations in \(a\) and \(b\). Solving: \(a=5,\ b=8\).
If p(4) = −7, the remainder when p(x) is divided by x − 4 is
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(2 t + 1\) is a factor of \(k t^{2} + t^{3} + 4 t - 2\).
Divide \(x^{3} - 7 x^{2} + 5 x + 17\) by \(x - 2\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(7\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(x^{2} - 5 x - 5\) and the remainder is \(7\). Check: \((x - 2)(x^{2} - 5 x - 5)+7=x^{3} - 7 x^{2} + 5 x + 17\).
A polynomial is divided by a polynomial of degree \(3\). What is the highest possible degree of the remainder?
The degree of the remainder is always less than the degree of the divisor, so at most \(3-1=2\). (A degree-0 remainder is a constant.)
Find the degree of the polynomial \(- x^{3} y z^{2} + 7 y^{2} z\).
Add the exponents of all the variables in each term; the degree of the polynomial is the largest of these sums: 6, 3. So the degree is \(6\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-4)=0\) so \(x + 4\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 4)(x + 1)(2 x - 3)\). Check by expanding.
The graph of a cubic polynomial must cross the x-axis at least
A cubic goes from one side of the axis to the other (odd degree), so it must cross the x-axis at least once.
Compared with a polynomial, the graph of a rational expression such as 1/x
Division by zero is not allowed, so a rational graph has a gap or asymptote where the denominator is 0.
Synthetic division is a shortcut for dividing a polynomial by
It only works for linear divisors of the form x − c (use x = −b/a idea for ax + b).
In checking a factor, a student finds p(c) = 5. The correct conclusion is
\(x-c\) is not a factor; the remainder is 5
A non-zero value means a non-zero remainder, so the divisor is not a factor.
The polynomial \(3 k + x^{4} - x^{3} - 5 x^{2} - 5 x\) leaves remainder \(-15\) when divided by \(x - 3\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(3)\). Substituting: \(3 k - 6=-15\), which gives \(k=-3\). Always substitute back to check.
The polynomial \(- k y^{2} + 2 y^{3} + 6 y + 1\) leaves remainder \(-10\) when divided by \(y + 1\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-1)\). Substituting: \(- k - 7=-10\), which gives \(k=3\). Always substitute back to check.
Which of the following is NOT a polynomial?
The exponent 3/2 is not a whole number. The other three have whole-number exponents (irrational coefficients are fine).
The volume of a rectangular box is \(44\) cubic units. The length is 7 more than the height and the width is 3 less than the height. Find the longest side of the box.

Let the height be \(h\). Volume \(=h^{3} + 4 h^{2} - 21 h=44\) gives \(h^{3} + 4 h^{2} - 21 h - 44=0\). Trying divisors of the constant term, \(h=4\) works, so the sides are \(4, 11, 1\). The other roots are negative, so they are rejected.
Find the remainder when \(t^{3} - 3 t^{2} + 4 t + 2\) is divided by \(t + 2\).
The divisor \(t + 2\) is zero when \(t=-2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-2)=-26\). (A common slip is to use \(p(2)\) = \(6\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
The polynomial \(- k x^{3} + 2 x^{4} - 5 x^{2} - 5 x - 3\) leaves remainder \(43\) when divided by \(x + 2\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-2)\). Substituting: \(8 k + 19=43\), which gives \(k=3\). Always substitute back to check.
Find the remainder when \(- x^{4} - 9 x^{3} - 4 x^{2} - x - 1\) is divided by \(x - 3\).

The divisor \(x - 3\) is zero when \(x=3\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(3)=-364\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-3)\) = \(128\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} + 3 x^{2} - 6 x - 8\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(-1)=0\), so \(x + 1\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(4, 2, -5\).
Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\). Multiply: \(x^{3} - x^{2} - 22 x + 40\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
Which of the following is a zero of \(x^{3} + 4 x^{2} - 7 x - 10\)?
\(a\) is a zero of \(p(x)\) exactly when \(p(a)=0\). Here \(p(-5)=0\); for the other values \(p(a)\neq 0\).
The degree of a polynomial in one variable is
the value of the leading coefficient
the highest power of the variable
the sum of all the coefficients
Look at the exponents of the variable and pick the largest: that is the degree.
Without long division, find the remainder when \(3 x^{4} - 3 x^{3} + 6 x^{2} + 5 x - 1\) is divided by \(x+1\).
Divisor \(x+1\) gives \(x=-1\). The remainder \(p(-1)=6\) is the alternating sum of the coefficients: no division needed.
Divide \(2 y^{3} - 10 y^{2} + 16 y - 6\) by \(y - 2\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(2\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 y^{2} - 6 y + 4\) and the remainder is \(2\). Check: \((y - 2)(2 y^{2} - 6 y + 4)+2=2 y^{3} - 10 y^{2} + 16 y - 6\).
A room has volume \(x^{3} + 14 x^{2} + 61 x + 84\) cubic feet and height \(x+7\) feet. Find the area of its floor.
\(\text{volume}=\text{area of floor}\times\text{height}\), so floor area = volume ÷ height. \(x^{3} + 14 x^{2} + 61 x + 84\) ÷ \(x+7\) = \(x^{2} + 7 x + 12\).
Find the remainder when \(3 t^{3} - 2 t^{2} - 6 t + 7\) is divided by \(3 t - 1\).
Set \(3 t - 1=0\): \(t=\frac{1}{3}\). Remainder \(=p(\frac{1}{3})=\frac{44}{9}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Find the remainder when \(2 t^{3} + 4 t^{2} + 2 t + 5\) is divided by \(5 t + 3\).
Set \(5 t + 3=0\): \(t=- \frac{3}{5}\). Remainder \(=p(- \frac{3}{5})=\frac{601}{125}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(t + 2\) is a factor of \(2 k + 2 t^{3} + 7 t^{2} + 5 t\).
Without long division, find the remainder when \(3 x^{3} + 3 x^{2} - x + 8\) is divided by \(x+1\).
Divisor \(x+1\) gives \(x=-1\). The remainder \(p(-1)=9\) is the alternating sum of the coefficients: no division needed.
The volume of a rectangular box is \(2160\) cubic units. The width is 3 times the height and the length is 2 more than the width. Find the height of the box.

Let the height be \(h\). Volume \(=9 h^{3} + 6 h^{2}=2160\) gives \(9 h^{3} + 6 h^{2} - 2160=0\). Trying divisors of the constant term, \(h=6\) works, so the sides are \(6, 18, 20\). The other roots are negative, so they are rejected.
In the division identity, the degree of the remainder is always
equal to the degree of the quotient
less than the degree of the divisor
greater than the degree of the dividend
equal to the degree of the divisor
Division stops only when what is left has smaller degree than the divisor.
Find the remainder when \(t^{4} + 3 t^{3} - 9 t^{2} + 9 t + 1\) is divided by \(t - 2\).
The divisor \(t - 2\) is zero when \(t=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=23\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(-61\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
The polynomial \(- k + 2 x^{3} - 6 x^{2} + 2 x\) leaves remainder \(-110\) when divided by \(x + 3\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-3)\). Substituting: \(- k - 114=-110\), which gives \(k=-4\). Always substitute back to check.
The polynomial \(3 k x^{2} + x^{4} - x^{3} - x - 1\) leaves remainder \(-4\) when divided by \(x + 1\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-1)\). Substituting: \(3 k + 2=-4\), which gives \(k=-2\). Always substitute back to check.
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(-5, -1, 0\).
Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\). Multiply: \(x^{3} + 6 x^{2} + 5 x\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-5)=0\) so \(x + 5\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 5)(x + 4)(x - 5)\). Check by expanding.
The y-intercept of the graph of y = p(x) is
The curve meets the y-axis when x = 0, so the height there is p(0), the constant term.
Find the remainder when \(2 x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 5 x - 1\) is divided by \(x + 2\).
The divisor \(x + 2\) is zero when \(x=-2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-2)=-7\). (A common slip is to use \(p(2)\) = \(45\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Divide \(2 x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 4 x + 8\) by \(x + 1\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(7\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 x^{2} + 3 x + 1\) and the remainder is \(7\). Check: \((x + 1)(2 x^{2} + 3 x + 1)+7=2 x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 4 x + 8\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-2)=0\) so \(x + 2\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 2)(2 x - 3)(x - 5)\). Check by expanding.
One zero of \(x^{3} - 8 x^{2} + 4 x + 48\) is \(-2\). Find the largest of the three zeros.
\(x--2\) is a factor (since \(p(-2)=0\)). Dividing leaves a quadratic whose roots are \(4\text{ and }6\). The largest zero is \(6\).
Find the remainder when \(x^{3} + 3 x^{2} + 9 x + 2\) is divided by \(x - 2\).
The divisor \(x - 2\) is zero when \(x=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=40\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(-12\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Divide \(2 t^{3} + 6 t^{2} - 6 t - 18\) by \(t + 3\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 t^{2} - 6\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((t + 3)(2 t^{2} - 6)=2 t^{3} + 6 t^{2} - 6 t - 18\).
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} - 10 x^{2} + 29 x - 20\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(4)=0\), so \(x - 4\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Divide \(t^{3} + 3 t^{2} - 6 t - 8\) by \(t - 2\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(t^{2} + 5 t + 4\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((t - 2)(t^{2} + 5 t + 4)=t^{3} + 3 t^{2} - 6 t - 8\).
One zero of \(x^{3} + 9 x^{2} + 26 x + 24\) is \(-4\). Find the largest of the three zeros.
\(x--4\) is a factor (since \(p(-4)=0\)). Dividing leaves a quadratic whose roots are \(-3\text{ and }-2\). The largest zero is \(-2\).
Find the remainder when \(x^{3} - x^{2} - 7 x + 3\) is divided by \(x^{2} + x - 2\).
The divisor is quadratic, so the Remainder Theorem (for x - c) cannot be used. By long division the quotient is \(x - 2\) and the remainder is \(- 3 x - 1\) (degree less than 2).
Divide \(2 x^{3} - 6 x^{2} - 4 x + 14\) by \(x - 3\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(2\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 x^{2} - 4\) and the remainder is \(2\). Check: \((x - 3)(2 x^{2} - 4)+2=2 x^{3} - 6 x^{2} - 4 x + 14\).
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} + 9 x^{2} + 14 x - 24\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(-6)=0\), so \(x + 6\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(2 x - 1\) is a factor of \(k x + x^{3} + x^{2} - 3\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(x - 1\) is a factor of \(- k x + 2 x^{3} - 6\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-3)=0\) so \(x + 3\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 3)(x + 1)(2 x - 1)\). Check by expanding.
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-5)=0\) so \(x + 5\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 5)(x - 3)(x - 4)\). Check by expanding.
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-3)=0\) so \(x + 3\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 3)(x - 3)(x - 4)\). Check by expanding.
Two linear factors of \(2 x^{3} + 9 x^{2} - 8 x - 15\) are \(2 x - 3\) and \(x + 1\). Find the third factor.

Multiply the two known factors: \(2 x^{2} - x - 3\). Divide the cubic by it: the quotient is \(x + 5\), the missing factor. Quick check: the product of the constants of the factors equals the constant term.
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} + 6 x^{2} + 3 x - 10\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(1)=0\), so \(x - 1\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
What is the name of the polynomial \(3 x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 4 x + 2\) according to its degree?
The highest power of \(x\) is \(3\), so the polynomial has degree \(3\): it is cubic.
The volume of a rectangular box is \(240\) cubic units. The length is 2 more than the height and the width is 1 less than the height. Find the height of the box.

Let the height be \(h\). Volume \(=h^{3} + h^{2} - 2 h=240\) gives \(h^{3} + h^{2} - 2 h - 240=0\). Trying divisors of the constant term, \(h=6\) works, so the sides are \(6, 8, 5\). The other roots are negative, so they are rejected.
Find the remainder when \(t^{4} - 2 t^{3} + 3 t^{2} - 2 t + 7\) is divided by \(5 t + 3\).
Set \(5 t + 3=0\): \(t=- \frac{3}{5}\). Remainder \(=p(- \frac{3}{5})=\frac{6151}{625}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Find the remainder when \(2 y^{4} - 8 y^{3} - 9 y^{2} - 3 y + 5\) is divided by \(y - 2\).
The divisor \(y - 2\) is zero when \(y=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=-69\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(71\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Find the remainder when \(x^{4} + 7 x^{3} + 8 x^{2} + 6 x + 2\) is divided by \(x - 2\).

The divisor \(x - 2\) is zero when \(x=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=118\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(-18\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
A polynomial whose highest power is 2 is called
Degree 1 is linear, degree 2 quadratic, degree 3 cubic.
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(2, -2, -1\).
Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\). Multiply: \(x^{3} + x^{2} - 4 x - 4\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
The volume of a rectangular box is \(270\) cubic units. The width is 1 more than the height and the length is 4 more than the height. Find the longest side of the box.

Let the height be \(h\). Volume \(=h^{3} + 5 h^{2} + 4 h=270\) gives \(h^{3} + 5 h^{2} + 4 h - 270=0\). Trying divisors of the constant term, \(h=5\) works, so the sides are \(5, 6, 9\). The other roots are negative, so they are rejected.
Divide \(2 t^{3} - 6 t + 1\) by \(t + 2\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(-3\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 t^{2} - 4 t + 2\) and the remainder is \(-3\). Check: \((t + 2)(2 t^{2} - 4 t + 2)+-3=2 t^{3} - 6 t + 1\).
Find the remainder when \(3 x^{3} + 4 x^{2} + x + 5\) is divided by \(2 x - 1\).
Set \(2 x - 1=0\): \(x=\frac{1}{2}\). Remainder \(=p(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{55}{8}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Two linear factors of \(x^{3} + 6 x^{2} + 3 x - 10\) are \(x + 5\) and \(x + 2\). Find the third factor.

Multiply the two known factors: \(x^{2} + 7 x + 10\). Divide the cubic by it: the quotient is \(x - 1\), the missing factor. Quick check: the product of the constants of the factors equals the constant term.
Find the remainder when \(x^{3} + 3 x^{2} + 5\) is divided by \(x^{2} - x + 2\).
The divisor is quadratic, so the Remainder Theorem (for x - c) cannot be used. By long division the quotient is \(x + 4\) and the remainder is \(2 x - 3\) (degree less than 2).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-2)=0\) so \(x + 2\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 2)(x - 1)(2 x - 5)\). Check by expanding.
The volume of a rectangular box is \(160\) cubic units. The length is 3 more than the height and the width is 1 less than the height. Find the longest side of the box.

Let the height be \(h\). Volume \(=h^{3} + 2 h^{2} - 3 h=160\) gives \(h^{3} + 2 h^{2} - 3 h - 160=0\). Trying divisors of the constant term, \(h=5\) works, so the sides are \(5, 8, 4\). The other roots are negative, so they are rejected.
If the remainder on dividing p(x) by d(x) is 0, then
d(x) is a factor of p(x)
Zero remainder means p(x) = d(x) · q(x): the division is exact.
The divisor is \(x + 1\), the quotient is \(x^{2} + x - 1\) and the remainder is \(-5\). Find the dividend.
dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder = \((x + 1)(x^{2} + x - 1)-5\) = \(x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 6\).
A room has volume \(x^{3} + 16 x^{2} + 81 x + 126\) cubic feet and height \(x+3\) feet. Find the area of its floor.
\(\text{volume}=\text{area of floor}\times\text{height}\), so floor area = volume ÷ height. \(x^{3} + 16 x^{2} + 81 x + 126\) ÷ \(x+3\) = \(x^{2} + 13 x + 42\).
Find the remainder when \(3 x^{3} - 8 x^{2} - 7 x - 8\) is divided by \(x - 1\).

The divisor \(x - 1\) is zero when \(x=1\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(1)=-20\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-1)\) = \(-12\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
The tickets sold in game number \(x\) are modelled by \(t(x)=x^{3} - 12 x^{2} + 27 x + 50\). How many tickets are sold in game \(10\)?
Game number \(10\) means \(x=10\): \(t(10)=120\). This number is also the remainder when \(t(x)\) is divided by \(x-10\).
Two linear factors of \(2 x^{3} + 7 x^{2} - 10 x - 24\) are \(2 x + 3\) and \(x - 2\). Find the third factor.

Multiply the two known factors: \(2 x^{2} - x - 6\). Divide the cubic by it: the quotient is \(x + 4\), the missing factor. Quick check: the product of the constants of the factors equals the constant term.
Without long division, find the remainder when \(- x^{4} - 6 x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 2 x - 8\) is divided by \(x+1\).
Divisor \(x+1\) gives \(x=-1\). The remainder \(p(-1)=0\) is the alternating sum of the coefficients: no division needed.
Divide \(x^{3} + 7 x^{2} + 11 x - 6\) by \(x + 3\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(-3\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(x^{2} + 4 x - 1\) and the remainder is \(-3\). Check: \((x + 3)(x^{2} + 4 x - 1)+-3=x^{3} + 7 x^{2} + 11 x - 6\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(3 y + 1\) is a factor of \(- k + y^{3} - 7 y^{2} - 5 y\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-5)=0\) so \(x + 5\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 5)(x + 3)(x - 6)\). Check by expanding.
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-6)=0\) so \(x + 6\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 6)(x - 1)(x - 2)\). Check by expanding.
Divide \(2 t^{3} - 7 t - 2\) by \(t - 2\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 t^{2} + 4 t + 1\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((t - 2)(2 t^{2} + 4 t + 1)=2 t^{3} - 7 t - 2\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(x - 3\) is a factor of \(- k x + x^{3} + 2 x^{2} + 3\).
The divisor is \(x - 2\), the quotient is \(x^{2} + 6 x - 2\) and the remainder is \(-2\). Find the dividend.
dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder = \((x - 2)(x^{2} + 6 x - 2)-2\) = \(x^{3} + 4 x^{2} - 14 x + 2\).
Find the degree of the polynomial \(7 x^{2} z^{2} - z\).
Add the exponents of all the variables in each term; the degree of the polynomial is the largest of these sums: 4, 1. So the degree is \(4\).
Find the remainder when \(2 y^{3} - y^{2} - y - 2\) is divided by \(2 y - 3\).
Set \(2 y - 3=0\): \(y=\frac{3}{2}\). Remainder \(=p(\frac{3}{2})=1\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
One zero of \(x^{3} - 4 x^{2} - x + 4\) is \(4\). Find the smallest of the three zeros.
\(x-4\) is a factor (since \(p(4)=0\)). Dividing leaves a quadratic whose roots are \(-1\text{ and }1\). The smallest zero is \(-1\).
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(5, 1, -5\).
Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\). Multiply: \(x^{3} - x^{2} - 25 x + 25\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(-3, -2, -1\).
Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\). Multiply: \(x^{3} + 6 x^{2} + 11 x + 6\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
The polynomial \(k y + 2 y^{3} - 2 y^{2} - 5\) leaves remainder \(-10\) when divided by \(y + 1\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-1)\). Substituting: \(- k - 9=-10\), which gives \(k=1\). Always substitute back to check.
If p(x) has degree 4 and q(x) has degree 2, the degree of p(x) + q(x) is
In a sum the higher degree wins, because the lower-degree terms cannot cancel the leading term.
Divide \(2 x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 6 x + 8\) by \(x + 2\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 x^{2} + x + 4\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((x + 2)(2 x^{2} + x + 4)=2 x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 6 x + 8\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(3 x - 1\) is a factor of \(k x + x^{3} - 7 x^{2} - 1\).
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(-3, -5, 4\).
Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\). Multiply: \(x^{3} + 4 x^{2} - 17 x - 60\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
Two linear factors of \(x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - x - 2\) are \(x - 1\) and \(x + 2\). Find the third factor.

Multiply the two known factors: \(x^{2} + x - 2\). Divide the cubic by it: the quotient is \(x + 1\), the missing factor. Quick check: the product of the constants of the factors equals the constant term.
Divide \(x^{3} - x^{2} - 11 x - 3\) by \(x + 2\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(7\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(x^{2} - 3 x - 5\) and the remainder is \(7\). Check: \((x + 2)(x^{2} - 3 x - 5)+7=x^{3} - x^{2} - 11 x - 3\).
Which of the following is a factor of \(2 x^{3} - 13 x^{2} + 16 x - 5\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(5)=0\), so \(x - 5\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Which of the following is a zero of \(2 x^{3} + x^{2} - 7 x - 6\)?
\(a\) is a zero of \(p(x)\) exactly when \(p(a)=0\). Here \(p(2)=0\); for the other values \(p(a)\neq 0\).
Find the remainder when \(x^{3} + x + 6\) is divided by \(x - 2\).
The divisor \(x - 2\) is zero when \(x=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=16\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(-4\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Find the remainder when \(3 x^{3} + 6 x^{2} + 2 x + 2\) is divided by \(3 x - 2\).
Set \(3 x - 2=0\): \(x=\frac{2}{3}\). Remainder \(=p(\frac{2}{3})=\frac{62}{9}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Find the remainder when \(3 y^{4} + 7 y^{3} + y^{2} + y + 4\) is divided by \(4 y + 1\).

Set \(2 y + 1=0\): \(y=- \frac{1}{2}\). Remainder \(=p(- \frac{1}{2})=\frac{9}{4}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} + 7 x^{2} + 2 x - 40\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(-5)=0\), so \(x + 5\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
The height (in feet) of a ball after \(t\) seconds is \(h(t)=- 16 t^{2} + 80 t + 5\). Find its height after \(1\) seconds.
\(h(1)=-16(1)^2+80(1)+5=69\). By the Remainder Theorem this is also the remainder of \(h(t)\) divided by \(t-1\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-6)=0\) so \(x + 6\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 6)(x + 2)(x + 1)\). Check by expanding.
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-6)=0\) so \(x + 6\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 6)(x + 5)(x - 5)\). Check by expanding.
Find the remainder when \(2 y^{3} - 5 y^{2} + 6 y - 3\) is divided by \(4 y + 2\).
Set \(4 y + 2=0\): \(y=- \frac{1}{2}\). Remainder \(=p(- \frac{1}{2})=- \frac{15}{2}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
The polynomial \(k x^{2} + x^{3} - 2\) leaves remainder \(-22\) when divided by \(x + 2\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-2)\). Substituting: \(4 k - 10=-22\), which gives \(k=-3\). Always substitute back to check.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(x + 1\) is a factor of \(- k x + 2 x^{3} - 5 x^{2} - 2\).
A polynomial of degree \(4\) is divided by a polynomial of degree \(3\). What is the degree of the quotient?
degree of quotient = degree of dividend − degree of divisor = \(4-3=1\).
The polynomial \(3 k + x^{3} + 4 x^{2} - 4 x\) leaves remainder \(27\) when divided by \(x + 3\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-3)\). Substituting: \(3 k + 21=27\), which gives \(k=2\). Always substitute back to check.
Divide \(2 x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 2 x + 15\) by \(x + 3\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 x^{2} - x + 5\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((x + 3)(2 x^{2} - x + 5)=2 x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 2 x + 15\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-6)=0\) so \(x + 6\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 6)(x + 4)(x + 1)\). Check by expanding.
Find the remainder when \(x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 2 x - 4\) is divided by \(3 x - 3\).
Set \(3 x - 3=0\): \(x=1\). Remainder \(=p(1)=-7\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
One zero of \(x^{3} + 5 x^{2} - 26 x - 120\) is \(-4\). Find the largest of the three zeros.
\(x--4\) is a factor (since \(p(-4)=0\)). Dividing leaves a quadratic whose roots are \(-6\text{ and }5\). The largest zero is \(5\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(t - 1\) is a factor of \(k + t^{3} - 3 t^{2} - 4 t\).
A room has volume \(x^{3} + 9 x^{2} + 23 x + 15\) cubic feet and height \(x+3\) feet. Find the area of its floor.
\(\text{volume}=\text{area of floor}\times\text{height}\), so floor area = volume ÷ height. \(x^{3} + 9 x^{2} + 23 x + 15\) ÷ \(x+3\) = \(x^{2} + 6 x + 5\).
Find the remainder when \(2 y^{3} - y^{2} + 4 y - 5\) is divided by \(y + 2\).

The divisor \(y + 2\) is zero when \(y=-2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-2)=-33\). (A common slip is to use \(p(2)\) = \(15\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(1, -2, -3\).
Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\). Multiply: \(x^{3} + 4 x^{2} + x - 6\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
The polynomial \(k x^{2} + 2 x^{3} + 6 x - 3\) leaves remainder \(13\) when divided by \(x - 2\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(2)\). Substituting: \(4 k + 25=13\), which gives \(k=-3\). Always substitute back to check.
Find the remainder when \(2 t^{3} - 2 t^{2} + 4 t + 1\) is divided by \(2 t + 1\).
Set \(2 t + 1=0\): \(t=- \frac{1}{2}\). Remainder \(=p(- \frac{1}{2})=- \frac{7}{4}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} - 13 x^{2} + 54 x - 72\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(6)=0\), so \(x - 6\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
A polynomial is divided by a polynomial of degree \(2\). What is the highest possible degree of the remainder?
The degree of the remainder is always less than the degree of the divisor, so at most \(2-1=1\). (A degree-0 remainder is a constant.)
What is the name of the polynomial \(t^{4} - 9 t^{3} + 8 t^{2} + 3 t - 9\) according to its degree?
The highest power of \(t\) is \(4\), so the polynomial has degree \(4\): it is bi-quadratic.
The area of a rectangle is \(3 x^{2} + 8 x + 5\) and its width is \(x + 1\). Find its length.
length = area ÷ width = \((3 x^{2} + 8 x + 5)\div(x + 1)=3 x + 5\).
The divisor is \(x - 3\), the quotient is \(x^{2} + 2 x - 1\) and the remainder is \(12\). Find the dividend.
dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder = \((x - 3)(x^{2} + 2 x - 1)+12\) = \(x^{3} - x^{2} - 7 x + 15\).
The polynomial \(k x + 2 x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 4\) leaves remainder \(62\) when divided by \(x - 3\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(3)\). Substituting: \(3 k + 68=62\), which gives \(k=-2\). Always substitute back to check.
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} + 6 x^{2} - 25 x - 150\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(-5)=0\), so \(x + 5\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Find the remainder when \(3 y^{4} + y^{3} - 2 y^{2} + 2 y + 1\) is divided by \(2 y - 2\).
Set \(2 y - 2=0\): \(y=1\). Remainder \(=p(1)=5\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Without long division, find the remainder when \(2 x^{3} - 7 x^{2} + 2 x - 8\) is divided by \(x+1\).
Divisor \(x+1\) gives \(x=-1\). The remainder \(p(-1)=-19\) is the alternating sum of the coefficients: no division needed.
The area of a rectangle is \(2 x^{2} + 5 x + 3\) and its width is \(x + 1\). Find its length.
length = area ÷ width = \((2 x^{2} + 5 x + 3)\div(x + 1)=2 x + 3\).
Find the remainder when \(x^{3} - 2 x^{2} + 3 x - 6\) is divided by \(x + 3\).

The divisor \(x + 3\) is zero when \(x=-3\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-3)=-60\). (A common slip is to use \(p(3)\) = \(12\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Two linear factors of \(x^{3} - 3 x^{2} - 18 x + 40\) are \(x + 4\) and \(x - 2\). Find the third factor.

Multiply the two known factors: \(x^{2} + 2 x - 8\). Divide the cubic by it: the quotient is \(x - 5\), the missing factor. Quick check: the product of the constants of the factors equals the constant term.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(t - 1\) is a factor of \(k t^{2} + t^{3} + 5 t + 2\).
Divide \(y^{3} + 5 y^{2} - 12 y + 8\) by \(y - 1\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(2\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(y^{2} + 6 y - 6\) and the remainder is \(2\). Check: \((y - 1)(y^{2} + 6 y - 6)+2=y^{3} + 5 y^{2} - 12 y + 8\).
One zero of \(x^{3} - 4 x^{2} - 20 x + 48\) is \(2\). Find the largest of the three zeros.
\(x-2\) is a factor (since \(p(2)=0\)). Dividing leaves a quadratic whose roots are \(-4\text{ and }6\). The largest zero is \(6\).
The polynomial \(3 k x + x^{3} + 6 x^{2} - 6\) leaves remainder \(-11\) when divided by \(x - 1\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(1)\). Substituting: \(3 k + 1=-11\), which gives \(k=-4\). Always substitute back to check.
Divide \(2 t^{3} + 3 t^{2} - 6 t - 11\) by \(t + 2\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(-3\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 t^{2} - t - 4\) and the remainder is \(-3\). Check: \((t + 2)(2 t^{2} - t - 4)+-3=2 t^{3} + 3 t^{2} - 6 t - 11\).
The tickets sold in game number \(x\) are modelled by \(t(x)=x^{3} - 9 x^{2} + 48 x + 74\). How many tickets are sold in game \(6\)?
Game number \(6\) means \(x=6\): \(t(6)=254\). This number is also the remainder when \(t(x)\) is divided by \(x-6\).
Which of the following is a factor of \(2 x^{3} - 5 x^{2} - 11 x - 4\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(4)=0\), so \(x - 4\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Two linear factors of \(2 x^{3} - x^{2} - 12 x - 9\) are \(x - 3\) and \(x + 1\). Find the third factor.

Multiply the two known factors: \(x^{2} - 2 x - 3\). Divide the cubic by it: the quotient is \(2 x + 3\), the missing factor. Quick check: the product of the constants of the factors equals the constant term.
Divide \(2 t^{3} - 2 t^{2} - 10 t + 4\) by \(t + 2\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 t^{2} - 6 t + 2\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((t + 2)(2 t^{2} - 6 t + 2)=2 t^{3} - 2 t^{2} - 10 t + 4\).
Divide \(x^{3} - 3 x^{2} + 5 x - 1\) by \(x - 1\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(2\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(x^{2} - 2 x + 3\) and the remainder is \(2\). Check: \((x - 1)(x^{2} - 2 x + 3)+2=x^{3} - 3 x^{2} + 5 x - 1\).
Find the remainder when \(t^{3} + 4 t^{2} - 4 t - 7\) is divided by \(2 t + 1\).
Set \(2 t + 1=0\): \(t=- \frac{1}{2}\). Remainder \(=p(- \frac{1}{2})=- \frac{33}{8}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Which of the following is a zero of \(x^{3} - 8 x^{2} + 17 x - 10\)?
\(a\) is a zero of \(p(x)\) exactly when \(p(a)=0\). Here \(p(5)=0\); for the other values \(p(a)\neq 0\).
Find the degree of the polynomial \(- 6 x^{2} y^{2} z^{2} - x^{2} y - 4 x^{2} z\).
Add the exponents of all the variables in each term; the degree of the polynomial is the largest of these sums: 3, 6, 3. So the degree is \(6\).
Find the remainder when \(t^{3} + 4 t^{2} + 5 t - 4\) is divided by \(3 t - 1\).
Set \(3 t - 1=0\): \(t=\frac{1}{3}\). Remainder \(=p(\frac{1}{3})=- \frac{50}{27}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-3)=0\) so \(x + 3\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 3)(x - 1)(x - 2)\). Check by expanding.
Find the remainder when \(3 x^{3} + 3 x^{2} + 8 x + 3\) is divided by \(x - 2\).
The divisor \(x - 2\) is zero when \(x=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=55\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(-25\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
The volume of a rectangular box is \(144\) cubic units. The width is 3 times the height and the length is 6 more than the width. Find the height of the box.

Let the height be \(h\). Volume \(=9 h^{3} + 18 h^{2}=144\) gives \(9 h^{3} + 18 h^{2} - 144=0\). Trying divisors of the constant term, \(h=2\) works, so the sides are \(2, 6, 12\). The other roots are negative, so they are rejected.
Find the remainder when \(2 x^{3} - 2 x - 8\) is divided by \(x + 2\).
The divisor \(x + 2\) is zero when \(x=-2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-2)=-20\). (A common slip is to use \(p(2)\) = \(4\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Find a polynomial with integer coefficients whose zeros are \(\frac{1}{2}, -4, -3\).

Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\) (for a fraction use a factor with integer coefficients, e.g. \(2x-1\) for \(\frac12\)). Multiply: \(2 x^{3} + 13 x^{2} + 17 x - 12\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
Find the remainder when \(y^{3} - 7 y^{2} + 2 y - 7\) is divided by \(2 y + 2\).
Set \(2 y + 2=0\): \(y=-1\). Remainder \(=p(-1)=-17\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
What is the name of the polynomial \(t^{3} - 4 t^{2} - t + 9\) according to its degree?
The highest power of \(t\) is \(3\), so the polynomial has degree \(3\): it is cubic.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(3 x - 1\) is a factor of \(2 k x^{2} + x^{3} - 3 x + 2\).
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(-1, 1, -3\).
Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\). Multiply: \(x^{3} + 3 x^{2} - x - 3\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
Find a polynomial with integer coefficients whose zeros are \(\frac{3}{2}, 5, 2\).

Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\) (for a fraction use a factor with integer coefficients, e.g. \(2x-1\) for \(\frac12\)). Multiply: \(2 x^{3} - 17 x^{2} + 41 x - 30\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
The area of a rectangle is \(x^{2} + 3 x + 2\) and its width is \(x + 2\). Find its length.
Find the remainder when \(2 z^{3} - 8 z^{2} - 6 z + 3\) is divided by \(z + 2\).

The divisor \(z + 2\) is zero when \(z=-2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-2)=-33\). (A common slip is to use \(p(2)\) = \(-25\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Find the remainder when \(3 x^{3} + 3 x^{2} - 3 x - 5\) is divided by \(x + 2\).

The divisor \(x + 2\) is zero when \(x=-2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-2)=-11\). (A common slip is to use \(p(2)\) = \(25\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-4)=0\) so \(x + 4\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 4)(x + 3)(2 x + 3)\). Check by expanding.
Find the remainder when \(y^{3} - y^{2} + 7 y + 7\) is divided by \(2 y - 1\).
Set \(2 y - 1=0\): \(y=\frac{1}{2}\). Remainder \(=p(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{83}{8}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Find the remainder when \(2 x^{4} - 6 x^{3} - 9 x^{2} - 8 x + 7\) is divided by \(x - 3\).

The divisor \(x - 3\) is zero when \(x=3\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(3)=-98\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-3)\) = \(274\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
The volume of a rectangular box is \(252\) cubic units. The width is 3 more than the height and the length is 5 more than the height. Find the longest side of the box.

Let the height be \(h\). Volume \(=h^{3} + 8 h^{2} + 15 h=252\) gives \(h^{3} + 8 h^{2} + 15 h - 252=0\). Trying divisors of the constant term, \(h=4\) works, so the sides are \(4, 7, 9\). The other roots are negative, so they are rejected.
Without long division, find the remainder when \(3 x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 4 x + 8\) is divided by \(x-1\).
Divisor \(x-1\) gives \(x=1\). The remainder \(p(1)=5\) is the sum of all the coefficients: no division needed.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(x + 1\) is a factor of \(2 k + x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 7 x\).
Find the remainder when \(x^{3} + 3 x^{2} + 4 x - 2\) is divided by \(x + 2\).
The divisor \(x + 2\) is zero when \(x=-2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-2)=-6\). (A common slip is to use \(p(2)\) = \(26\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
\(a x^{2} + x^{3} - 2 x - 1\) and \(2 a + x^{3} + 2 x^{2} + 3 x\) leave the same remainder when divided by \(x + 1\). Find \(a\).
Which of the following is a factor of \(2 x^{3} + 5 x^{2} - 4 x - 3\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(-3)=0\), so \(x + 3\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Find the remainder when \(2 y^{3} + 7 y^{2} + 4\) is divided by \(y - 2\).
The divisor \(y - 2\) is zero when \(y=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=48\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(16\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
The divisor is \(x + 1\), the quotient is \(3 x^{2} - 2 x + 1\) and the remainder is \(7\). Find the dividend.
dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder = \((x + 1)(3 x^{2} - 2 x + 1)+7\) = \(3 x^{3} + x^{2} - x + 8\).
The polynomial \(- k + 2 x^{4} - 5 x^{3} - 4 x^{2} - x\) leaves remainder \(-13\) when divided by \(x - 3\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(3)\). Substituting: \(- k - 12=-13\), which gives \(k=1\). Always substitute back to check.
Find the remainder when \(2 x^{3} - 6 x^{2} + 11 x - 11\) is divided by \(x^{2} - x + 2\).
The divisor is quadratic, so the Remainder Theorem (for x - c) cannot be used. By long division the quotient is \(2 x - 4\) and the remainder is \(3 x - 3\) (degree less than 2).
Which of the following is a zero of \(x^{3} - 8 x^{2} - 3 x + 90\)?
\(a\) is a zero of \(p(x)\) exactly when \(p(a)=0\). Here \(p(-3)=0\); for the other values \(p(a)\neq 0\).

The polynomial \(- k y + y^{3} - 6 y^{2} - 1\) leaves remainder \(-27\) when divided by \(y + 2\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-2)\). Substituting: \(2 k - 33=-27\), which gives \(k=3\). Always substitute back to check.
Find the remainder when \(y^{3} + 4 y^{2} + 2 y - 5\) is divided by \(y - 2\).
The divisor \(y - 2\) is zero when \(y=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=23\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(-1\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
The volume of a rectangular box is \(1296\) cubic units. The width is 2 times the height and the length is 6 more than the width. Find the height of the box.

Let the height be \(h\). Volume \(=4 h^{3} + 12 h^{2}=1296\) gives \(4 h^{3} + 12 h^{2} - 1296=0\). Trying divisors of the constant term, \(h=6\) works, so the sides are \(6, 12, 18\). The other roots are negative, so they are rejected.
Find the remainder when \(x^{3} - 5 x^{2} + 5 x + 2\) is divided by \(x - 2\).
The divisor \(x - 2\) is zero when \(x=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=0\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(-36\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-4)=0\) so \(x + 4\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 4)(x + 2)(x - 6)\). Check by expanding.
A room has volume \(x^{3} + 14 x^{2} + 59 x + 70\) cubic feet and height \(x+2\) feet. Find the area of its floor.
\(\text{volume}=\text{area of floor}\times\text{height}\), so floor area = volume ÷ height. \(x^{3} + 14 x^{2} + 59 x + 70\) ÷ \(x+2\) = \(x^{2} + 12 x + 35\).
Divide \(2 y^{3} - 8 y^{2} + 7 y + 9\) by \(y - 2\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(7\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 y^{2} - 4 y - 1\) and the remainder is \(7\). Check: \((y - 2)(2 y^{2} - 4 y - 1)+7=2 y^{3} - 8 y^{2} + 7 y + 9\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(x + 1\) is a factor of \(2 k x + 2 x^{3} + 3 x^{2} + 5\).
Find the remainder when \(2 x^{4} - 7 x^{3} - 9 x^{2} - 5 x - 6\) is divided by \(x + 3\).

Find the remainder when \(3 z^{4} + 5 z^{3} + 9 z^{2} + 8 z - 1\) is divided by \(z + 3\).

The divisor \(z + 3\) is zero when \(z=-3\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-3)=164\). (A common slip is to use \(p(3)\) = \(482\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(0, -2, -5\).

Which of the following is a zero of \(x^{3} + 4 x^{2} - 36 x - 144\)?

Divide \(y^{3} + y^{2} + 4 y + 4\) by \(y + 1\). Find the quotient.
Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(y^{2} + 4\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((y + 1)(y^{2} + 4)=y^{3} + y^{2} + 4 y + 4\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(y - 1\) is a factor of \(- k + 2 y^{3} - 4 y^{2} - 3 y\).
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} - 13 x + 12\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(-4)=0\), so \(x + 4\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Which of the following is a factor of \(2 x^{3} - 13 x^{2} + 22 x - 8\)?

Find the remainder when \(x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 2 x + 3\) is divided by \(x - 2\).
The divisor \(x - 2\) is zero when \(x=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=-1\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(-25\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
If \(x + 1\) and \(x - 2\) are both factors of \(a x^{2} + b x + x^{3} + 6\), find \(a\).
\(p(-1)=0\) and \(p(2)=0\) give two linear equations in \(a\) and \(b\). Solving: \(a=-4,\ b=1\).

Find the value of \(k\) for which \(x - 1\) is a factor of \(- k + x^{3} + 5 x^{2} + 7 x\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-2)=0\) so \(x + 2\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 2)(x + 1)(x - 4)\). Check by expanding.
Find the remainder when \(2 y^{3} + 2 y^{2} - 6 y + 4\) is divided by \(y + 1\).
The divisor \(y + 1\) is zero when \(y=-1\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-1)=10\). (A common slip is to use \(p(1)\) = \(2\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
The polynomial \(2 k x^{2} + x^{3} + 5 x + 2\) leaves remainder \(-40\) when divided by \(x + 2\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-2)\). Substituting: \(8 k - 16=-40\), which gives \(k=-3\). Always substitute back to check.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(2 x + 1\) is a factor of \(- k + x^{3} + 4 x^{2} - 4 x\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-4)=0\) so \(x + 4\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 4)(x - 1)(x - 4)\). Check by expanding.
Without long division, find the remainder when \(- x^{4} + 2 x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 5 x - 7\) is divided by \(x+1\).
Divisor \(x+1\) gives \(x=-1\). The remainder \(p(-1)=-7\) is the alternating sum of the coefficients: no division needed.
Find the remainder when \(3 y^{3} + 2 y^{2} + 2 y + 5\) is divided by \(3 y + 1\).
Set \(3 y + 1=0\): \(y=- \frac{1}{3}\). Remainder \(=p(- \frac{1}{3})=\frac{40}{9}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Divide \(x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 3\) by \(x - 1\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(x^{2} - 3 x - 3\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((x - 1)(x^{2} - 3 x - 3)=x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 3\).
The polynomial \(k x^{2} + 2 x^{3} - 5 x + 2\) leaves remainder \(32\) when divided by \(x - 3\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(3)\). Substituting: \(9 k + 41=32\), which gives \(k=-1\). Always substitute back to check.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(x - 3\) is a factor of \(k + 2 x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 4 x\).
Divide \(2 x^{3} + 8 x^{2} - 6\) by \(x + 1\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 x^{2} + 6 x - 6\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((x + 1)(2 x^{2} + 6 x - 6)=2 x^{3} + 8 x^{2} - 6\).
The polynomial \(k x^{3} + x^{4} - 3 x^{2} + x + 5\) leaves remainder \(-33\) when divided by \(x + 2\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-2)\). Substituting: \(7 - 8 k=-33\), which gives \(k=5\). Always substitute back to check.
The divisor is \(x - 2\), the quotient is \(2 x^{2} - 4 x - 5\) and the remainder is \(7\). Find the dividend.
dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder = \((x - 2)(2 x^{2} - 4 x - 5)+7\) = \(2 x^{3} - 8 x^{2} + 3 x + 17\).
\(a x^{2} + x^{3} - 4 x + 4\) and \(2 a + x^{3} + x^{2}\) leave the same remainder when divided by \(x + 1\). Find \(a\).
Find the remainder when \(2 z^{3} - 3 z^{2} + 6 z - 5\) is divided by \(z - 2\).
The divisor \(z - 2\) is zero when \(z=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=11\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(-45\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Find the remainder when \(2 y^{3} - 5 y^{2} + 5 y - 6\) is divided by \(3 y - 3\).
Set \(3 y - 3=0\): \(y=1\). Remainder \(=p(1)=-4\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Find the remainder when \(3 t^{3} - 8 t^{2} - 3 t + 2\) is divided by \(t - 1\).
The divisor \(t - 1\) is zero when \(t=1\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(1)=-6\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-1)\) = \(-6\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-4)=0\) so \(x + 4\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 4)(x - 1)(x - 6)\). Check by expanding.
Find the remainder when \(3 x^{4} - 4 x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 3 x + 5\) is divided by \(x - 2\).
The divisor \(x - 2\) is zero when \(x=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=11\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(63\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
If \(x - 1\) and \(x + 3\) are both factors of \(a x^{2} + b x + x^{3} + 12\), find \(b\).
\(p(1)=0\) and \(p(-3)=0\) give two linear equations in \(a\) and \(b\). Solving: \(a=-2,\ b=-11\).
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} + 4 x^{2} + x - 6\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(1)=0\), so \(x - 1\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Divide \(2 x^{3} - x^{2} - 13 x - 6\) by \(x + 2\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 x^{2} - 5 x - 3\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((x + 2)(2 x^{2} - 5 x - 3)=2 x^{3} - x^{2} - 13 x - 6\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(t + 1\) is a factor of \(2 k t^{2} + 2 t^{3} + 6 t - 2\).
The polynomial \(k + 2 x^{3} + 6 x^{2} - 3 x\) leaves remainder \(3\) when divided by \(x - 1\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(1)\). Substituting: \(k + 5=3\), which gives \(k=-2\). Always substitute back to check.
Find the remainder when \(2 y^{3} + 5 y^{2} + 7 y + 3\) is divided by \(2 y - 1\).
Set \(2 y - 1=0\): \(y=\frac{1}{2}\). Remainder \(=p(\frac{1}{2})=8\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} + 5 x^{2} - 8 x - 12\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(-1)=0\), so \(x + 1\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} + 7 x^{2} - 36\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(-6)=0\), so \(x + 6\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Find the remainder when \(x^{3} - 3 x^{2} + 4 x - 9\) is divided by \(x^{2} + 3\).
The divisor is quadratic, so the Remainder Theorem (for x - c) cannot be used. By long division the quotient is \(x - 3\) and the remainder is \(x\) (degree less than 2).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-3)=0\) so \(x + 3\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 3)(x + 1)(2 x - 3)\). Check by expanding.
Find a polynomial with integer coefficients whose zeros are \(\frac{1}{2}, 5, -3\).

Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\) (for a fraction use a factor with integer coefficients, e.g. \(2x-1\) for \(\frac12\)). Multiply: \(2 x^{3} - 5 x^{2} - 28 x + 15\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(y - 2\) is a factor of \(2 k y^{2} + y^{3} + 2 y + 4\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(2 t + 1\) is a factor of \(- k t^{2} + t^{3} - 6 t - 7\).
Which of the following is a zero of \(x^{3} + x^{2} - 32 x - 60\)?
\(a\) is a zero of \(p(x)\) exactly when \(p(a)=0\). Here \(p(-2)=0\); for the other values \(p(a)\neq 0\).
Without long division, find the remainder when \(x^{4} + 4 x^{3} - x^{2} - 4 x - 5\) is divided by \(x+1\).
Divisor \(x+1\) gives \(x=-1\). The remainder \(p(-1)=-5\) is the alternating sum of the coefficients: no division needed.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(2 y + 1\) is a factor of \(k + 2 y^{3} - 7 y^{2} + y\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(2 y + 1\) is a factor of \(k + 2 y^{3} + 4 y^{2}\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(2 t - 1\) is a factor of \(2 k + t^{3} - 6 t^{2} - 5 t\).
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(y - 3\) is a factor of \(k + 2 y^{3} - 5 y^{2}\).
Find the remainder when \(2 x^{4} + x^{3} + 2 x^{2} + 7 x - 7\) is divided by \(x - 2\).
The divisor \(x - 2\) is zero when \(x=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=55\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(11\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-6)=0\) so \(x + 6\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 6)(x + 4)(x - 2)\). Check by expanding.
Two linear factors of \(x^{3} - 4 x^{2} - 9 x + 36\) are \(x - 3\) and \(x + 3\). Find the third factor.

Multiply the two known factors: \(x^{2} - 9\). Divide the cubic by it: the quotient is \(x - 4\), the missing factor. Quick check: the product of the constants of the factors equals the constant term.
Find the remainder when \(3 y^{3} - 7 y^{2} - 5 y - 3\) is divided by \(y - 2\).

The divisor \(y - 2\) is zero when \(y=2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(2)=-17\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-2)\) = \(-45\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Find the remainder when \(3 x^{3} + 2 x^{2} + x + 2\) is divided by \(3 x - 1\).
Set \(3 x - 1=0\): \(x=\frac{1}{3}\). Remainder \(=p(\frac{1}{3})=\frac{8}{3}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} + 12 x^{2} + 44 x + 48\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(-4)=0\), so \(x + 4\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Two linear factors of \(2 x^{3} + 3 x^{2} - 30 x + 25\) are \(2 x - 5\) and \(x - 1\). Find the third factor.

Multiply the two known factors: \(2 x^{2} - 7 x + 5\). Divide the cubic by it: the quotient is \(x + 5\), the missing factor. Quick check: the product of the constants of the factors equals the constant term.
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-2)=0\) so \(x + 2\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 2)(x - 3)(x - 4)\). Check by expanding.
A room has volume \(x^{3} + 17 x^{2} + 94 x + 168\) cubic feet and height \(x+4\) feet. Find the area of its floor.
\(\text{volume}=\text{area of floor}\times\text{height}\), so floor area = volume ÷ height. \(x^{3} + 17 x^{2} + 94 x + 168\) ÷ \(x+4\) = \(x^{2} + 13 x + 42\).
The tickets sold in game number \(x\) are modelled by \(t(x)=x^{3} - 3 x^{2} + 12 x + 20\). How many tickets are sold in game \(2\)?
Game number \(2\) means \(x=2\): \(t(2)=40\). This number is also the remainder when \(t(x)\) is divided by \(x-2\).
One zero of \(x^{3} - 14 x^{2} + 63 x - 90\) is \(5\). Find the smallest of the three zeros.
\(x-5\) is a factor (since \(p(5)=0\)). Dividing leaves a quadratic whose roots are \(3\text{ and }6\). The smallest zero is \(3\).
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(-3, -1, -2\).
Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\). Multiply: \(x^{3} + 6 x^{2} + 11 x + 6\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
Divide \(2 y^{3} - 6 y^{2} + 8 y - 4\) by \(y - 1\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 y^{2} - 4 y + 4\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((y - 1)(2 y^{2} - 4 y + 4)=2 y^{3} - 6 y^{2} + 8 y - 4\).
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(5, 0, 2\).
Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\). Multiply: \(x^{3} - 7 x^{2} + 10 x\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
Which of the following is a zero of \(x^{3} - 5 x^{2} - 16 x + 80\)?
\(a\) is a zero of \(p(x)\) exactly when \(p(a)=0\). Here \(p(5)=0\); for the other values \(p(a)\neq 0\).
Without long division, find the remainder when \(x^{3} + 7 x^{2} + 3 x + 1\) is divided by \(x\).
Divisor \(x\) gives \(x=0\). The remainder \(p(0)=1\) is the constant term: no division needed.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(y + 2\) is a factor of \(2 k + 2 y^{3} - 6 y^{2} + y\).
Find a polynomial with integer coefficients whose zeros are \(- \frac{1}{2}, -1, -3\).

Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\) (for a fraction use a factor with integer coefficients, e.g. \(2x-1\) for \(\frac12\)). Multiply: \(2 x^{3} + 9 x^{2} + 10 x + 3\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
The divisor is \(x - 4\), the quotient is \(3 x^{2} - x + 6\) and the remainder is \(-2\). Find the dividend.
dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder = \((x - 4)(3 x^{2} - x + 6)-2\) = \(3 x^{3} - 13 x^{2} + 10 x - 26\).
Find the remainder when \(y^{3} + y^{2} - 8 y - 4\) is divided by \(y - 3\).
The divisor \(y - 3\) is zero when \(y=3\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(3)=8\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-3)\) = \(2\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Find a polynomial with integer coefficients whose zeros are \(\frac{1}{2}, -4, -1\).

Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\) (for a fraction use a factor with integer coefficients, e.g. \(2x-1\) for \(\frac12\)). Multiply: \(2 x^{3} + 9 x^{2} + 3 x - 4\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
Find the remainder when \(2 x^{3} + 3 x^{2} - 4\) is divided by \(3 x + 2\).
Set \(3 x + 2=0\): \(x=- \frac{2}{3}\). Remainder \(=p(- \frac{2}{3})=- \frac{88}{27}\). For a divisor \(ax+b\) use \(x=-b/a\).
Find the remainder when \(2 x^{3} - 7 x^{2} + 3 x - 5\) is divided by \(x - 1\).
The divisor \(x - 1\) is zero when \(x=1\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(1)=-7\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-1)\) = \(-17\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Find the remainder when \(2 x^{3} + x + 2\) is divided by \(x + 2\).

The divisor \(x + 2\) is zero when \(x=-2\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-2)=-16\). (A common slip is to use \(p(2)\) = \(20\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
The height (in feet) of a ball after \(t\) seconds is \(h(t)=- 16 t^{2} + 96 t + 5\). Find its height after \(3\) seconds.
\(h(3)=-16(3)^2+96(3)+5=149\). By the Remainder Theorem this is also the remainder of \(h(t)\) divided by \(t-3\).
What is the name of the polynomial \(2 t^{3} - t^{2} + t + 7\) according to its degree?
The highest power of \(t\) is \(3\), so the polynomial has degree \(3\): it is cubic.
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-4)=0\) so \(x + 4\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 4)(2 x - 5)(x - 3)\). Check by expanding.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(y - 1\) is a factor of \(k y^{2} + 2 y^{3} + 4 y - 5\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-2)=0\) so \(x + 2\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 2)(x - 2)(x - 6)\). Check by expanding.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(x + 3\) is a factor of \(- k x^{2} + 2 x^{3} + x - 6\).
Divide \(x^{3} + 8 x^{2} + 9 x - 9\) by \(x + 2\). Find the quotient. (The remainder is \(-3\).)

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(x^{2} + 6 x - 3\) and the remainder is \(-3\). Check: \((x + 2)(x^{2} + 6 x - 3)+-3=x^{3} + 8 x^{2} + 9 x - 9\).
Divide \(y^{3} + 2 y - 12\) by \(y - 2\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(y^{2} + 2 y + 6\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((y - 2)(y^{2} + 2 y + 6)=y^{3} + 2 y - 12\).
The tickets sold in game number \(x\) are modelled by \(t(x)=x^{3} - 3 x^{2} + 48 x + 50\). How many tickets are sold in game \(6\)?
Game number \(6\) means \(x=6\): \(t(6)=446\). This number is also the remainder when \(t(x)\) is divided by \(x-6\).
Without long division, find the remainder when \(- x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 8 x + 7\) is divided by \(x\).
Divisor \(x\) gives \(x=0\). The remainder \(p(0)=7\) is the constant term: no division needed.
The volume of a rectangular box is \(72\) cubic units. The length is 5 more than the height and the width is 2 less than the height. Find the height of the box.

Let the height be \(h\). Volume \(=h^{3} + 3 h^{2} - 10 h=72\) gives \(h^{3} + 3 h^{2} - 10 h - 72=0\). Trying divisors of the constant term, \(h=4\) works, so the sides are \(4, 9, 2\). The other roots are negative, so they are rejected.
Find the remainder when \(x^{3} + 2 x - 1\) is divided by \(x - 1\).
The divisor \(x - 1\) is zero when \(x=1\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(1)=2\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-1)\) = \(-4\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Find the remainder when \(3 z^{3} - 4 z^{2} - z + 8\) is divided by \(z + 1\).
The divisor \(z + 1\) is zero when \(z=-1\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(-1)=2\). (A common slip is to use \(p(1)\) = \(6\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Divide \(2 y^{3} + 9 y^{2} + 13 y + 12\) by \(y + 3\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 y^{2} + 3 y + 4\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((y + 3)(2 y^{2} + 3 y + 4)=2 y^{3} + 9 y^{2} + 13 y + 12\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-2)=0\) so \(x + 2\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 2)(2 x - 1)(x - 4)\). Check by expanding.
Find the remainder when \(2 y^{3} - 3 y^{2} + 4 y + 2\) is divided by \(y - 3\).
The divisor \(y - 3\) is zero when \(y=3\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(3)=41\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-3)\) = \(-91\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-2)=0\) so \(x + 2\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 6)\). Check by expanding.
What is the name of the polynomial \(- 2 x^{3} - x^{2} + 6 x - 6\) according to its degree?
The highest power of \(x\) is \(3\), so the polynomial has degree \(3\): it is cubic.
One zero of \(x^{3} + 4 x^{2} - x - 4\) is \(-1\). Find the largest of the three zeros.
\(x--1\) is a factor (since \(p(-1)=0\)). Dividing leaves a quadratic whose roots are \(-4\text{ and }1\). The largest zero is \(1\).
Find a polynomial with whose zeros are \(-4, -1, 3\).
Each zero \(a\) gives a factor \(x-a\). Multiply: \(x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 11 x - 12\). Any non-zero multiple has the same zeros.
Find the remainder when \(y^{4} - 3 y^{3} + 8 y^{2} - 2 y - 8\) is divided by \(y - 3\).
The divisor \(y - 3\) is zero when \(y=3\). By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is \(p(3)=58\). (A common slip is to use \(p(-3)\) = \(232\): the sign of c is opposite to the sign in the divisor.)
The volume of a rectangular box is \(440\) cubic units. The width is 3 more than the height and the length is 6 more than the height. Find the height of the box.

Let the height be \(h\). Volume \(=h^{3} + 9 h^{2} + 18 h=440\) gives \(h^{3} + 9 h^{2} + 18 h - 440=0\). Trying divisors of the constant term, \(h=5\) works, so the sides are \(5, 8, 11\). The other roots are negative, so they are rejected.
The polynomial \(k y^{3} + y^{4} - 2 y^{2} + y - 3\) leaves remainder \(-6\) when divided by \(y + 1\). Find \(k\).
Remainder \(=p(-1)\). Substituting: \(- k - 5=-6\), which gives \(k=1\). Always substitute back to check.
Which of the following is a zero of \(x^{3} - 9 x^{2} + 26 x - 24\)?
\(a\) is a zero of \(p(x)\) exactly when \(p(a)=0\). Here \(p(2)=0\); for the other values \(p(a)\neq 0\).
Try values that divide the constant term. \(p(-2)=0\) so \(x + 2\) is a factor; divide to get a quadratic and factorize it. Result: \((x + 2)(2 x - 1)(x - 1)\). Check by expanding.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \(x + 1\) is a factor of \(k + 2 x^{3} - x^{2} + 3 x\).
Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} - 3 x^{2} - 16 x - 12\)?
A factor \(x-c\) needs \(p(c)=0\). Test: \(p(-2)=0\), so \(x + 2\) is a factor. The others leave a non-zero remainder.
Without long division, find the remainder when \(2 x^{4} + 6 x^{3} - 2 x^{2} - 8 x + 2\) is divided by \(x-1\).
Divisor \(x-1\) gives \(x=1\). The remainder \(p(1)=0\) is the sum of all the coefficients: no division needed.
Divide \(2 t^{3} - 6 t^{2} + 6 t - 4\) by \(t - 2\). Find the quotient.

Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the whole divisor, subtract, repeat. The quotient is \(2 t^{2} - 2 t + 2\) and the remainder is \(0\). Check: \((t - 2)(2 t^{2} - 2 t + 2)=2 t^{3} - 6 t^{2} + 6 t - 4\).
